packs.title: Park, Bay & Pacific
packs.promise: Explore San Diego’s landmark park, maritime stories and Pacific coast.

q.s: Look at what an animal’s space provides.
st: Choose one open habitat along a route suited to your mobility after entering the Zoo.
Observe three habitat features offering cover, movement or rest; seeing the animal itself is unnecessary.
Use the interpretive label to connect one feature with the animal’s needs, keeping your observation separate from the label’s explanation.

q.s: Let the upper floors tell a different story from the storefronts.
st: Choose a comfortable daytime block near Fifth and Island using marked crossings.
Collect three upper-story details in notes: a window shape, a cornice edge and a decorative repeat.
Choose one that makes the block recognizable without a shop sign.

q.s: Connect an exhibit with a human task.
st: Choose one open exhibit along a suitable museum route after admission.
Read or listen to its interpretation and identify a task someone performed with the displayed object or space.
Write a two-sentence label of your own: one sourced fact about the task and one question you still have. Do not invent a quotation or service member’s story.

packs.title: Balboa Park, Garden to Gallery
packs.promise: Follow the park’s central paths through living collections, public art and exposition architecture.

q.s: Write what you left out and why.
st: Choose a dry viewpoint where the water and its surroundings are visible.
Draw a tiny reflection scene, leaving one deliberate blank space where water breaks the image.
Write what you left out and why.

q.s: Choose the process you would most like to watch and describe the tool you expect it to use as a question.
st: Visit the open courtyard and read three studio signs or public displays.
Collect three different media or making processes identified by the artists.
Choose the process you would most like to watch and describe the tool you expect it to use as a question.

q.s: Note which curve guides a person around the space.
st: Observe from a dry public path and find three circles or curved shapes in the fountain and plaza.
Rank them from smallest to largest.
Note which curve guides a person around the space.
